proposals.before: He then expelled Zhang Qiu from Jingyuan, Yang Shouzhong from Yangzhou, and Man Cun from Fengzhou, seized their territories, and petitioned to install his sons and brothers as governors, which the court was powerless to prevent.
proposals.after: He then expelled Zhang Qiu from Jingyuan, Yang Shouzhong from Yang Prefecture, and Man Cun from Fengzhou, seized their territories, and petitioned to install his sons and brothers as governors, which the court was powerless to prevent.
proposals.reason: 洋州 is Yang Prefecture (Yangzhou in Hanzhong), not the Jiangnan prefecture commonly spelled Yangzhou (揚州).

proposals.before: In the seventh month of that year, Taiyuan's army reached Hezhong; Jipeng together with the palace eunuch Jing Xuan's son Jisheng forced the imperial carriage to go to Fengxiang; Emperor Zhaozong said: "Taiyuan's army has not yet arrived; the imperial carriage must not be moved lightly; I together with the princes will hold fast within the inner palace; you are to pacify the capital; if Taiyuan truly arrives, I can control them by strategy."
proposals.after: In the seventh month of that year, Taiyuan's army reached Hezhong; Jipeng together with the palace eunuch Jing Xuan's son Jisheng pressed the imperial carriage to go to Fengxiang; Emperor Zhaozong said: "Taiyuan's army has not yet arrived; the imperial carriage must not be moved lightly; I together with the princes will hold fast within the inner palace; you are to pacify the capital; if Taiyuan truly arrives, I can control them by strategy."
proposals.reason: The Chinese 迫 marks coercion, but the immediately following refusal shows the flight was not completed in this sentence; 'forced ... to go' overstates the outcome.

proposals.before: Yet in commanding troops he observed no discipline at all; at mealtimes he would go to the kitchens and often sit on the ground; even those who held the keys were addressed as Acting Grand Guardian — a far cry from the martial renown of Zhou Yafu and Feng Yi.
proposals.after: Yet in commanding troops he observed no discipline at all; at mealtimes he would go to the kitchens and often sit on the ground; even those who held the keys inside and outside were addressed as Minister of Works and Grand Guardian — a far cry from the martial renown of Zhou Yafu and Feng Yi.
proposals.reason: 司空太保 is the paired court titles Sikong and Taibao, not a single Acting Grand Guardian; 內外 is also omitted.

proposals.before: Maozhen soon received an imperial ordinance promoting him to Grand Preceptor of the First Rank, acting Grand Commandant, concurrent Palace Attendant, commander of the Four Garrisons Northern Court campaign army, and military commissioner of the Zhangyi army.
proposals.after: Maozhen soon, by delegated imperial authority, conferred on him the titles of Grand Preceptor of the First Rank, acting Grand Commandant, concurrent Palace Attendant, commander of the Four Garrisons Northern Court campaign army, and military commissioner of the Zhangyi Army.
proposals.reason: Chinese 承制加 has Maozhen conferring these Zhangyi titles on Congyan, whose Jingzhou posting occupies the preceding sentence; the English makes Maozhen the promotee.

proposals.before: Maozhen soon received an imperial ordinance adding the titles of Grand Preceptor with equal ceremonial to the Three Excellencies, acting Grand Commandant, and concurrent Palace Attendant, commander of the Four Garrisons Northern Court campaign army, and military commissioner of the Zhangyi Army.
proposals.after: Maozhen soon by delegated authority added the titles of Grand Preceptor with equal ceremonial to the Three Excellencies, acting Grand Commandant, and concurrent Palace Attendant, commander of the Four Garrisons Northern Court campaign army, and military commissioner of the Zhangyi Army.
proposals.reason: Literal received-an-ordinance-adding hides 承制 and leaves the beneficiary ambiguous.

proposals.before: At the end of Tang he was a capital garrison commander of Fengxiang; Maozhen memorialized him as military commissioner of Fu Prefecture; he rose in office to concurrent Palace Attendant.
proposals.after: At the end of Tang he was a garrison commander of Fengxiang; Maozhen memorialized him as military commissioner of Fu Prefecture; he rose in office to concurrent Palace Attendant.
proposals.reason: 都將 is a garrison commander, not a capital garrison commander; 都 does not mean capital here.

proposals.before: When the Liang founder besieged Fengxiang, Maoxun camped at Qishan; the founder baited him with a weak force and sent Kong Qian with elite troops to seize Fuzhou and capture his whole family; Maoxun then submitted to Liang, took the name Zhou Yi, and was made campaigning marshal at headquarters.
proposals.after: When the Liang founder besieged Fengxiang, Maoxun camped at Qishan; the founder baited him with a weak force and sent Kong Qian with elite troops to seize Fuzhou and capture his whole family; Maoxun then submitted to Liang, took the name Zhou Yi, and was appointed adjutant (xingjun sima) of the Marshal's headquarters.
proposals.reason: 元帥府行軍司馬 is the campaign adjutant/sima of the marshal's headquarters, not a campaigning marshal.

proposals.before: Soon he was made senior general of the Golden Crow Guard and assisted Wang Zan at Jingdian; when Zan posted him at the western camp, Zhuangzong attacked and defeated him, and he was demoted to senior general of the Left Guard.
proposals.after: Soon he was made senior general of the Jinwu Guard and assisted Wang Zan at Jingdian; when Zan posted him at the western camp, Zhuangzong attacked and defeated him, and he was demoted to senior general of the Left Guard.
proposals.reason: 金吾 is the Jinwu (Imperial Insignia) Guard, not a Golden Crow Guard.

proposals.after: Maoxun was Maozhen's younger male cousin.
proposals.reason: 從弟 specifically means a younger male cousin, which the literal rendering already captures.

proposals.before: During Kaiping, Liang general Liu Zhijun rebelled from Tongzhou and fled to Fengxiang; Maozhen's territory was too cramped to hold him, so he borrowed troops to probe Lingwu and seize pasturelands.
proposals.after: During Kaiping, Liang general Liu Zhijun rebelled from Tongzhou and fled to Fengxiang; Li Maozhen's territory was too cramped to hold him, so he borrowed troops to probe Lingwu and seize pasturelands.
proposals.reason: Chinese names 李茂貞 in full; the idiomatic English drops the surname Li.

proposals.before: Zhu was then appointed Grand Preceptor of the First Rank.
proposals.after: Zhu was then appointed Grand Preceptor with ceremonial equal to the Three Excellencies.
proposals.reason: 開府儀同三司 is Kaifu Yitong Sansi, not Grand Preceptor of the First Rank; the literal rendering is accurate.

proposals.before: In the summer of the fourth year of Tiancheng Zhu died, and the court appointed his younger brother Cheng acting commissioner of the Shuofang army.
proposals.after: In the summer of the fourth year of Tiancheng, Zhu died, and the court appointed his younger brother Cheng acting commissioner of the Shuofang army.
proposals.reason: Missing comma fuses the reign year Tiancheng with the personal name Zhu.

proposals.before: Soon the Prince of Jin sent Zhou Dewei with fifty thousand troops from Bin and Feng to attack Xiazhou; Renfu held out for over a month until Liang reinforcements arrived and Dewei withdrew; the founder was pleased and specially promoted him to acting Grand Guardian and Tongping Zhangshi.
proposals.after: Soon the Martial Emperor of Later Tang sent Zhou Dewei with fifty thousand troops from Bin and Feng to attack Xiazhou; Renfu held out for over a month until Liang reinforcements arrived and Dewei withdrew; the founder was pleased and specially promoted him to acting Grand Guardian and Tongping Zhangshi.
proposals.reason: Chinese 後唐武皇 is the Martial Emperor of Later Tang, not the Prince of Jin.

proposals.before: Li Yichao has already been removed and appointed acting commissioner for observation of Yan Prefecture; he is to be compelled to proceed to his post at once.
proposals.after: Li Yichao has already been appointed acting commissioner for observation of Yan Prefecture; he is to be compelled to proceed to his post at once.
proposals.reason: Chinese 除 here is the standard verb of appointment, not removal; the literal rendering 'removed and appointed' reverses the office action.

decisions.reason: s0011 names 洋州, the Hanzhong command, not 揚州; English Yangzhou normally denotes the Jiangnan prefecture, so Yang Prefecture is the needed disambiguation.
迫 marks coercion, but Zhaozong's immediate refusal and the later riot show the carriage did not go to Fengxiang in this sentence; forced ... to go overstates the outcome.

decisions.reason: 內外持管鑰者 is omitted, and 司空太保 is the pair Sikong and Taibao, not the single title Acting Grand Guardian.

decisions.reason: 承制加 makes Maozhen the granter, and 彰義軍 follows Congyan's Jingzhou posting, so Maozhen is not the promotee; the proposal still mistranslates 開府儀同三司 as Grand Preceptor of the First Rank.

decisions.after: Maozhen soon by delegated authority added to him the titles of opening an office with equal ceremonial to the Three Excellencies, acting Grand Commandant, and concurrent Palace Attendant, commander of the Four Garrisons Northern Court campaign army, and military commissioner of the Zhangyi Army.
decisions.reason: 承制加 is delegated conferral on Congyan, not Maozhen receiving an ordinance; the proposal restores 承制 but still leaves the beneficiary unnamed and keeps Grand Preceptor for 開府儀同三司.

decisions.reason: 鳳翔都將 is a Fengxiang garrison commander; 都 is the unit prefix, not the capital.

decisions.after: When the Liang founder besieged Fengxiang, Maoxun camped at Qishan; the founder baited him with a weak force and sent Kong Qian with elite troops to seize Fuzhou and capture his whole family; Maoxun then submitted to Liang, took the name Zhou Yi, and was appointed campaign adjutant of the Marshal's headquarters.
decisions.reason: 元帥府行軍司馬 is the campaign adjutant of the marshal's headquarters, not a campaigning marshal; the proposed parenthetical gloss is accurate but awkward in idiomatic English.
金吾上將軍 is the Jinwu Guard; Golden Crow confuses 金吾 with 金烏.
從弟 is a younger male cousin, but English cousin is accurate enough here; the extra age and sex markers are already in the literal field.
李茂貞 is the same man already called Maozhen in this chapter; restoring the surname is a stylistic preference, not a semantic error.

decisions.after: Zhu was then appointed to the rank of opening an office with ceremonial equal to the Three Excellencies.
decisions.reason: 開府儀同三司 is one prestige rank, ceremonial equality with the Three Excellencies, not Grand Preceptor (太師); copying Grand Preceptor from the literal still invents that office.
The Chinese pauses after 天成四年夏 before 洙卒; without the comma, Tiancheng Zhu can be read as one name.
The actor is 後唐武皇, the Martial Emperor of Later Tang; Prince of Jin is not in this sentence.
